newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX dragged off at start with futures, U.S..
newsitem.headline: German DAX dragged off at start with futures, U.S..

text.p: Germany's fell in early bourse trading as they were dragged lower by the falling equity futures market and weak sentiment emerging from the U.S.

The DAX-30 index of leading German shares fell 43.19 points, down 1.30 percent, to 3,272.74 in early dealings. March DAX futures, due to expire on Friday, fell 34.0 points to 3,275.0, exerting a negative effect on the cash market.
Dealers also blamed lower U.S. Treasuries and a fall in the Dow U.S. share index overnight for the weakness. "All in all, there is a lot of pressure on the market today," one said.
Aside from the regular meeting of the Bundesbank council meeting later today, dealers said there was enough potential for uncertainty later on to keep investors sidelined.
US Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan is due later to testify before the Joint Economic Committee, while U.S. trade data could have an impact on the dollar, currently trading at 1.755 marks.
The main market focus was the restart of trade in Thyssen and Krupp-Hoesch after two days of suspension related to Krupp's attempt to produce a merger of their steel businesses.
Thyssen rose 33.20 marks, nearly 10 percent, to 380 marks while Krupp shares gained 15 percent to 313 marks.
Drugs group Schering climbed 5.25 marks, 3.36 percent, to 161.50 on continued positive reaction to its move on Wednesday to raise its forecast for 1997 results.
A number of stocks suffered profit-taking after recent strong runs.
Software group SAP was down 8.30 marks to 264.0, while a number of shares in the financial sector were lower. Dresdner lost 1.85 marks to 53.80 early on.
